summary: A 1925 D-6 cupola lookout on the Rogue River National Forest, used as a WWII aircraft warning post, NRHP-listed in 2000, and still standing but not regularly staffed.

facts.status_note: Vacant/not actively staffed in recent years; occasional Forest Service use

access.note: Reached via Forest Roads 6510, 6515 and 530 north of Union Creek, OR; rough road, high-clearance recommended, short hike at end

visit.trail_note: Short hike from end of FR 530

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Rogue River National Forest)

events.note: District fire plan proposes a lookout line to Hershberger Mountain
Earlier camp on the mountain predates the lookout structure
End of the period of significance for fire-detection use (1925-1943) per NRHP nomination; served as WWII aircraft warning station
Listed on National Register of Historic Places, December 29, 2000
Refurbished in the 1980s per onX/Hiking Project summary (exact year not specified)
Refurbished with new roof, shutters, glass, and paint

evidence.supports: Not actively staffed in recent years
evidence.quote: Hershberger Lookout is a cupola structure constructed in 1925. Also located on the Rogue River National Forest, it has not been actively staffed in recent years.
It was built in 1925 and was listed on the National Register of Historic Places on December 29, 2000.

evidence.supports: D-6 cupola cabin replaced earlier 1917 camp
evidence.quote: This D-6 cupola cabin, built in 1925, replaced an earlier camp dating from 1917.

evidence.supports: Design details, period of significance 1925-1943, privy abandoned, catwalk history
evidence.quote: Built in 1925, Hershberger Mountain Lookout is a standard "D-6" cupola-style lookout structure with a wood frame and a wood-shingled, hipped roof

evidence.supports: Lower floor as living quarters, ladder to cupola
evidence.quote: served as the living quarters, with stove, table, cupboards, bed, and other furniture. A ceiling-hinged ladder from the lower floor reaches the fire-spotting observatory in the second-story cupola.

evidence.supports: Current function vacant; privy long abandoned

evidence.quote: It replaced a two-sided catwalk, built in the 1960s, that enclosed the east and south sides.

evidence.supports: WWII aircraft warning use, refurbished 1980s and 2012, still occasional FS use, access route
evidence.quote: The Hershberger Mountain fire lookout is a D-6 cupola-type structure that was built in 1925, served as an aircraft warning station during WW2, was refurbished in the 1980s and 2012, and still sees occasional use by the Forest Service.

evidence.supports: 1913 proposal for lookout line to Hershberger Mountain
evidence.quote: It is proposed to build a line to Herschberger Mountain and this point will be used as a lookout.
The lookout underwent refurbishing, a new roof, shutters, glass, paint and other needed repairs.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com notes an earlier camp from 1917 predating the 1925 structure; all sources agree the lookout building itself dates to 1925, so no real conflict.

notes_for_editor: Good multi-source agreement on build date, design, and NRHP listing. The 'refurbished in the 1980s' date is vague (onX source only gives decade); no need to correct the brief's current record, which already matches these facts closely. Fact-check 2026-10-04: the 1913 fire-plan sentence was footnoted to source 1 (NHLR) but the supporting quote is from source 6 (weebly); corrected to [^6]. The story said the design was standard for 'Region 6 (then District 1)' lookouts, which inverts the actual history per the NRHP form (it was District Six, later renamed Region Six); corrected. The vacant/period-of-significance sentence cited source 6 (weebly), which does not support it; dropped, kept source 4 (NRHP) only. The living-quarters/ladder sentence copied the NRHP form's wording too closely; rewritten. The views sentence (Crater Lake, Thielsen, Bailey, McLoughlin, Shasta) had no footnote though it is directly supported by source 5 (Hiking Project); added [^5]. Spot-checked the Osborne firefinder alidade and three-sided catwalk claims directly against the NRHP document text; both confirmed verbatim.
